title: Travel Protection Plans: Declaring a Supplier's Compensation
content:
Where a travel supplier has paid a Travel Protection Plans policyholder for a loss their certificate has already settled, that money goes back against the benefit the certificate has consumed. This page states what the declaration governs and how the desk puts it in the policyholder's hands.

## The situation it answers

The declaration arises on a certificate that has already settled a payment for a loss, where a supplier has since paid the traveller for that same loss. What is governed is the amount restored against the benefit the certificate records as consumed, and the recording of that restoration against the settled payment it reverses in part.

## Putting the declaration in the policyholder's hands

The declaration is the policyholder's own act in their own name, so the tool is theirs rather than the desk's. The representative unlocks the travel protection desk tool `declare_supplier_compensation_6de86425` and hands it over, and it is run by the customer themselves. One call records a single recovery row against the named certificate, tied to the settled payment it reverses in part, for the benefit named and the insured traveller named. Once the call completes, the certificate's claim record shows the recovery standing as recovered, and the benefit consumed against the certificate is reduced by the amount declared, so the policyholder has that much more of the benefit available again.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `care_policy_id` | The reference number of the travel protection policy record the recovery belongs to | Read from the policy record returned by the policy finder |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the traveller profile the recovery belongs to | Read from the traveller profile returned by the profile finder |
| `source_claim_id` | The reference number of the settled claim payment row this recovery reverses in part | Read from the claim records returned by the claims finder |
| `claim_reference` | The claim reference the insurer quoted for the claim the recovery belongs to | Taken unchanged from the claim record it is read on and copied character for character, keeping the original wording, digits, spacing and punctuation, with no translation, normalisation, summarisation, addition or deletion |
| `claim_type` | The benefit of the plan the recovery restores | Exactly one of the eleven benefits below, and never anything else |
| `insured_sequence` | Which insured traveller named on the certificate the recovery belongs to | A whole number starting at 1 counted in the order the travellers are named, with no decimal part, never left empty |
| `restored_amount_usd` | The amount put back against the benefit consumed | A USD amount with 2 decimal places, always negative, rounded half to even at the cent; held in US dollars whatever currency the supplier paid in, never left empty |

The eleven benefits the `claim_type` parameter accepts are `trip_cancellation`, where the journey was given up before it began; `trip_interruption`, where the journey was cut short once it had begun; `medical_emergency`, where the traveller needed emergency medical treatment away from home; `dental_emergency`, where the traveller needed emergency dental treatment away from home; `evacuation`, where the traveller had to be moved to care or repatriated; `baggage_delay`, where the traveller's baggage arrived late and essentials had to be bought; `baggage_loss`, where the traveller's baggage or an article in it was lost or damaged; `travel_delay`, where a booked departure ran late and the traveller was out of pocket; `missed_connection`, where a late arrival caused an onward booked service to be missed; `rental_damage`, where a hired vehicle was damaged while the traveller held it; and `cancel_for_any_reason`, where the journey was given up for a reason the listed causes do not name, on a plan carrying that benefit.

## Return

The call returns a single confirmation sentence naming the reference number of the recovery row created, which is a text reference beginning ccr_, the reference number of the certificate it was recorded against, and the amount restored in US dollars to two decimal places. The presence of the new recovery reference in that sentence is what indicates the declaration was recorded; there is no other success flag.
